beats.text: How long does sex actually last? Scientists used a stopwatch.
Five hundred couples in five countries timed themselves for four weeks.
The median, from start of intercourse to finish: five point four minutes.
But it varied a lot. Some couples were under three and a half minutes, others over ten.
And sex therapists? They rated three to seven minutes as perfectly adequate.
So, shorter than the movies. And totally normal. The clock was never the point.

sources: Waldinger, Quinn, Dilleen et al. (2005). A multinational population survey of intravaginal ejaculation latency time. Journal of Sexual Medicine 2(4). 491 men in stable relationships (NL, ES, TR, UK, US), stopwatch over 4 weeks; median IELT 5.4 min; 14% median below 3:20, 26% above 10:00. Via Wikipedia (IELT).
Corty & Guardiani (2008). Canadian and American sex therapists' perceptions of normal and abnormal ejaculatory latencies. Journal of Sexual Medicine 5(5). 3-7 minutes rated adequate, 7-13 desirable.
